priorFindingsVerification.status: resolution INCOMPLETE -- a new, equally serious gap found one level deeper
priorFindingsVerification.note: The try/catch around payViaFacilitator genuinely closes the ORIGINAL in-process-exception gap for the common case. But it introduces two new, unwrapped failure modes never addressed anywhere in the spec's SHALL/Edge-Case/Acceptance-Criteria text: (1) the disbursement_uncertain follow-up append itself is a plain fs.appendFileSync (ledger.js:20-24) that can itself throw, leaving a 'provisioning' row with NO terminal follow-up and a NON-stale (cleanly-released) lock -- a third terminal state the state machine never names and for which reconciliation is never triggered; (2) reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's own on-chain RPC lookup, invoked at the start of the NEXT issuance attempt, can itself throw, and the spec only ever describes its two SUCCESS outcomes, never this failure. See FIND-301.

priorFindingsVerification.status: resolution PARTIALLY complete -- the specific manifest question is answered correctly, but a new ambiguity was found
priorFindingsVerification.note: The replay-blocklist is correctly scoped to 'previously-verified, CREDITED' rows only, so a txHash appearing in an already-rejected row correctly does NOT count as already-credited (a transiently-rejected-then-later-finalized real transaction is not wrongly blacklisted). However, the Edge Cases' own 'logged as a replay attempt' language for rejected replays is never defined as either an out-of-band log or a NEW loans.jsonl append -- and if the latter, it risks corrupting the last-write-wins convention every other computation in this spec depends on. Separately, no canonical loans.jsonl row schema is ever given, and the generic txHash field name is never structurally distinguished between disbursement-side and repayment-side rows. See FIND-302.

priorFindingsVerification.status: resolution INCOMPLETE -- the internal contradiction is fixed, but the enforcement mechanism itself is unverifiable against real code
priorFindingsVerification.note: The prior contradiction between the kill-switch SHALL and an adjacent Edge Case is genuinely resolved. But evaluateColdStartKillSwitch has NO Tier-0 structural proof obligation anywhere in the 48-item verification-architecture.md requiring the REAL REQ-106 issuance implementation to actually call it -- the only backing proof obligation (PROP-105g) is a Tier-1 pure-function test plus a Tier-2 test wired against 'a MOCKED REQ-106 issuance call,' never a structural read of the real call site (contrast PROP-106d/PROP-106i, which DO demand this for other REQ-106 wiring facts). This means the kill-switch can remain a computed flag nobody checks in production. See FIND-303.

priorFindingsVerification.status: resolution INCOMPLETE -- the debt-proportional formula is correct, but its composition-point description omits a required pipeline step
priorFindingsVerification.note: adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt's own arithmetic (debt-proportional, clamped at 0) is correct and well-tested (PROP-109b/f). But its stated insertion point ('AFTER filterProductiveCitizens's own output and BEFORE computeColonySurplusUsd') never mentions readCitizenBalances -- the effectful, coordinator-run step anicca-agent-spawn's CURRENT REQ-101 uses to attach the balance_i figure this pure function needs to already exist to reduce. Confirmed via grep: zero mentions of readCitizenBalances anywhere in this feature's own spec docs. See FIND-304.

REQ-106's own Acceptance Criteria (lines 858-864) now explicitly excludes REQ-108/109's per-loan lock from its own two-phase append, and a new Lock-key disambiguation paragraph (lines 804-813) plus a dedicated Tier-0 structural check (PROP-106i) make the distinction independently verifiable. No contradiction remains.

Every dollar-denominated pure function this feature introduces (computeLenderAvailableUsd, sumOutstandingPrincipalUsd, sumRecentGojoGiftsUsd, computeLoanCapUsd, total_due_usd) now explicitly applies the established .toFixed(6) money-precision convention, consistently, in EARS text, Edge Cases, and every Acceptance Criterion/PROP that asserts an exact numeric value.
